title: Pluggable eviction and decorators
idea: An extensible cache adds behaviour by new classes only: policies plug into `EvictionPolicy`, decorators wrap `Cache`, and a builder wires them from configuration.
points: A new policy implements `EvictionPolicy`; `BoundedCache` is never edited.
`CountingCache` wraps any `Cache`; `TtlCache` wraps a store of stamped values.
A builder holds the options, validates them once, and stacks the layers.
An injected clock lets expiry tests jump time instead of sleeping.

code.title: Add LFU without edits
code.caption: The same workload under LRU and LFU. The core from the class design page is pasted unchanged at the bottom.

walk.text: Pick a policy by name; the cache code is identical for both.
Wrap the bounded cache in a counting decorator and print evictions.
home is read often, promo was read last; then a third key arrives.
LFU tracks a use count per key and groups keys by count.
The victim is the oldest key in the lowest-count group.
A use moves the key from its old group to the next one.
The decorator counts hits and misses, then delegates every call.

code.title: Builder and TTL
code.caption: A builder adds expiry by wrapping the store. The fake clock is a long the demo moves by hand.

walk.text: Configure capacity, a 30-second TTL and a fake clock, then build.
Read one millisecond before expiry and exactly at expiry.
A negative TTL is refused at build time, before any use.
Defaults: capacity 1,000, LRU, no expiry, the system clock, a no-op listener.
Without TTL, return the plain store; with it, wrap the store.
Each stored value carries its own expiry time.
An expired entry is removed on read and reported as a miss.

pitfalls: Lazy expiry keeps unread dead entries; add a sweeper if capacity matters.
Plain LFU keeps old favourites forever; age the counts so new keys survive.
Validate options in `build()`, not during the first `put` in production.

quiz.q: Which line does LfuPlugin print for the LFU run's eviction?
quiz.why: home has four uses and promo two. LFU drops the key with the fewest uses, so promo goes even though it was read last.

takeaway: Extend with new policies and decorators; leave the core store untouched.
